summary: Describes a model that divides the RFC Editor's work into four functions, including the RFC Series Editor and the Independent Submission Editor. It was informational and was replaced by RFC 6548 and RFC 6635.

eli5.summary: The group that publishes RFCs has many jobs. This splits them among different roles so each has a clear owner.

questions: what is the rfc series editor
subtitle: Organizing the RFC editing, publishing and series management into four specialized roles.

tldr.problem: The RFC Editor role had grown too large for a single person, requiring coordination across multiple functions without clear organizational structure.
tldr.mechanism: The model divides responsibility into four distinct roles: the RFC Series Editor (policy and oversight), Independent Submission Editor (non-IETF track documents), RFC Production Center (editing and formatting), and RFC Publisher (announcement and maintenance).
tldr.outcome: This structure enabled clearer accountability, professional support, and succession planning. The model was refined in later RFCs 6548 and 6635.

facts.label: RFC Series Editor term
facts.value: Five years with no restrictions on renewals

today: This RFC describes Version 1 of the RFC Editor model. It was obsoleted by RFC 6548 and RFC 6635, which refined the model and adjusted the organizational structure.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The RFC Series is the permanent record of Internet technical standards. For decades it was edited by a single person, but as the Internet grew, the RFC Editor's work expanded into a large, complex operation with overlapping responsibilities that required coordination among many people.

This RFC describes a new organizational model that divides the RFC Editor's work into four distinct functions, each with clear responsibilities. The goal is to provide better operational support, enable succession planning, maintain quality while reducing costs, and increase transparency about how the RFC process works.
sections.eli5: The RFC Editor job was too much for one person. This explains how to split the job into four specialized teams that work together.

sections.title: The Four RFC Editor Functions
sections.content:
The model divides the RFC Editor into four functions:

RFC Series Editor provides executive leadership and policy oversight. This person faces the community, works with the Internet Architecture Board (IAB) and the IETF Administrative Oversight Committee (IAOC) on contractual matters, and chairs the RFC Series Advisory Group.

Independent Submission Editor reviews and approves documents submitted outside the normal IETF stream. This role maintains technical quality for submissions from anyone, working with an optional advisory board.

RFC Production Center is a contractor who edits documents to comply with style standards, assigns RFC numbers, communicates with authors and protocol registries, and prepares documents for publication.

RFC Publisher announces and makes RFCs available online, maintains the errata system, provides backups, stores records, and authenticates documents for legal purposes.
sections.eli5: The leader sets policy and talks to the community. One person handles documents from outside the main process. A team edits everything to make it look nice and assigns numbers. Another team publishes the documents and keeps copies safe.

sections.title: Roles and Qualifications
sections.content:
The RFC Series Editor must be a senior technology professional with deep IETF knowledge, executive management experience, excellent English skills, editorial expertise, and the ability to work independently. The RFC can be filled through a Request for Proposal (RFP) process or through nomination and confirmation by the IAB.

The Independent Submission Editor needs broad technical knowledge across Internet technologies, editorial skills, good standing in the technical community, and the ability to work effectively with authors and advisory boards. The IAB selects this person after seeking community input.

The RFC Production Center and RFC Publisher are selected through competitive RFP processes run by the IAOC. The model allows functions to be combined or separated based on operational needs.
sections.eli5: The leader needs deep knowledge of Internet standards and good management skills. The independent submissions editor is chosen because they know many technologies and write well. The other two roles go to whoever can do the best job for a good price.

sections.title: Governance and Advisory Groups
sections.content:
The RFC Series Advisory Group (RSAG) provides expert guidance to the RFC Series Editor on long-term developments and operational issues affecting the RFC Series. Its members serve staggered three-year terms and are appointed by the IAB for their expertise and interest in the RFC Series; they do not represent particular organizations or streams.

When disagreements arise between the functions, parties first seek informal resolution. If needed, the RFC Series Editor can decide operational matters. For major contractual issues, the IAD (Internet Administrative Director) and IAOC resolve them with advice from the RFC Series Editor.

The Independent Submission Stream Editorial Board is an optional group that advises the Independent Submission Editor on technical quality for independent submissions.
sections.eli5: Wise people meet regularly to give advice to the leader about long-term changes and big problems. If someone disagrees about how something should work, they first talk it over, and if they still can't agree, the leader decides. For money and contracts, the business side makes those decisions.

sections.title: Status Today
sections.content: RFC 6548 and RFC 6635 superseded this version of the RFC Editor model with updates and refinements. This document remains a landmark in the evolution of the RFC Series, establishing the principle that the RFC Editor function is too large and complex to be a single role, and that clear organizational structure, with defined responsibilities and oversight, is essential to maintaining the RFC Series' quality and accessibility.
sections.eli5: This model was replaced by two newer RFCs that made improvements. But the main idea—splitting the job into four teams—stayed the same.
